reservoir_ep04_001.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_001.text: On Day One Thousand Thirty-eight, the basin's calendar meeting began with an empty chair. Fu Lian had booked the morning interval around her grain work, but the cart that brought her from the lower station was late. Liu Tong, the baker from the western household turn, sat beside the empty place with both hands under his sleeves. Tian Yu arrived under his accepted shift exchange and looked at the chair as if its absence might make the room easier. Qiu asked everyone to begin with the actual public times already available.

reservoir_ep04_002.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_002.text: Liu needed an earlier draw on market mornings because his ovens began before the lower household turn reached its last users. His present late turn made him choose between cooling bread and carrying water after work. He had offered this account at the earlier public interval, with private names withheld. Today he was willing to identify his own household. Fu's grain deliveries created the opposite conflict. The room had two possible counterparts to a time exchange, and neither person had yet agreed to have the visitor decide for them.

reservoir_ep04_003.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_003.text: Tian placed the public grain dispatch correction on the table. Qiu read its dates aloud, then asked who had measured the household's actual waiting interval. Liu had his own record, while Fu's remained in her folder on the delayed cart. The difference could not be answered by adding a neat number to Tian's source. He looked disappointed but left the space open. Yue remembered how pleased he had been to carry a useful paper here. The paper was useful; it simply did not describe everything the room wanted to know.

reservoir_ep04_004.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_004.text: Liu complained that the grain house always arrived with better paper than the households did. Tian stiffened. He had spent a real traded shift preparing the copy and wanted its work recognized. Qiu asked Liu whether he meant the copy was inaccurate. He said no; he meant people without polished records seemed to be treated as late even when they had waited first. Yue asked him which receiving act would demonstrate that feeling concretely. He pointed to the empty chair and said Fu's lost hour was about to become another blank.

reservoir_ep04_005.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_005.text: They left Fu's offered time comparison pending instead of making the empty chair prove either neglect or agreement. Qiu moved to the public questions whose sources were present. Tian relaxed enough to read the corrected dispatch line, carefully preserving the difference between prepared packet time and actual departure. Liu listened, then admitted that one of his own copied dates used the earlier heading. The correction would help his account too. Tian's pleasure returned slowly. A disagreement at the table had not required either of them to lose all usefulness.

reservoir_ep04_006.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_006.text: Fu arrived before the posted interval ended, carrying a grain slip creased nearly through at its fold. The carrier's cart had stopped behind a fallen ordinary branch, then taken the accepted longer approach. Her actual delay was marked on its receiving note. She apologized for the lost meeting time and immediately asked which facts had already been compared. Qiu supplied the current list. Nobody asked her to tell the whole road story before her water question could count. Yue moved the spare cup toward her without touching the private folder.

reservoir_ep04_007.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_007.text: Fu's brother had agreed to one limited grain-shift exchange, not every market morning. The neighbor who had fetched their water during three earlier collisions now had her own care appointment and could no longer help on those dates. Fu laid the offered household calendar beside Liu's oven hours. The turn quantities were not the immediate problem. The available times were. Tian drew separate horizontal lines on a waste sheet and waited for both household owners to correct them. The simple drawing made the overlap visible enough that nobody needed to call it somebody's lack of resolve.

reservoir_ep04_008.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_008.text: Liu offered to discuss exchanging the two specific market-morning turns for a trial period. Fu wanted to check the current delivery dates and her brother's agreement before accepting. An exchange that helped this week could become difficult when deliveries moved again. Qiu named a review date and asked which exact turns the households would put under it. Yue watched the offer become smaller and more practical. It was tempting to describe the matching difficulties as proof that the valley had found its natural solution. The next delivery could change that neat story.

reservoir_ep04_009.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_009.text: A different cooperative member proposed holding Fu's usual quantity in a checked covered buffer so the family could collect it after paid weighing. That would keep the present turn order but require real handling, containers and a finite operating appointment. The water would still be drawn from Fu's accepted allocation at its original time, rather than added to the basin's available supply. Fu liked the steadiness. Liu liked not having to revise the public roster. Qiu asked who would pay and which qualified worker would accept the actual handling before discussing either preference further.

reservoir_ep04_010.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_010.text: The current water-assistance fund held twenty-four copper actually received from its members. Eighteen had paid six completed ordinary worker-day equivalents at three each, leaving six. A bounded buffer trial could use that remainder: three for one equivalent of qualified handling, two for inspected covered jars and one for an ordinary carrying tray. A turn exchange would leave the six unspent for a later ratified maintenance decision. Qiu set both amounts beside the proposals. Neither plan created water, and the cheaper one did not automatically meet everyone's actual hours better.

reservoir_ep04_011.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_011.text: The households wanted the proposals checked before their next overlapping work morning. Qiu offered the available receiving interval and asked Yue whether she could help with one accepted comparison while her grain dates remained intact. The work was a specific ordinary contribution she could consent to, not a transfer of institutional authority. Her retained winter-city terms still controlled which records she could request. The basin's receiver would decide whether the offered household calendars could be shown for this purpose. Fu kept her folder closed until that boundary was clear.

reservoir_ep04_012.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_012.text: On Day One Thousand Thirty-nine, Yue returned to her fourth accepted grain day. The meeting had left real questions, but the granary still needed its numbered work. Zhou asked Tian to begin with the current blank and let Yue finish the dispatch comparison. Their earlier argument with Liu had not changed the scale's ordinary behavior. At midday Tian said he had been unfairly angry about the empty chair. Yue said anger could signal an effort whose purpose had become unclear. He could ask for the purpose before making the absence into a personal insult.

reservoir_ep04_013.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_013.text: The day ended with another three-copper wage, bringing Yue's accepted grain earnings to twelve. Tian showed her a little crust Liu had left for the clerk after hearing the date correction. He had almost refused it, then decided it was an ordinary offered snack rather than payment for favorable testimony. They shared it at the public table. Its hard edge scraped Yue's thumb and made her laugh at the disproportionate care they had given the argument compared with the bread. Some tensions could ease through conversation and a small kindness without erasing their cause.

reservoir_ep04_014.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_014.text: On Day One Thousand Forty, Qiu received the two household proposals for the next comparison. Fu's brother had consented to the specified work dates, and Liu's household had checked its own oven calendar. The offered accounts still contained private matters unrelated to either plan. Qiu kept them covered. She would give Yue only the scope appropriate to her actual incoming arrangement and the households' present consent. Their problem had become sufficiently concrete that losing a detail could change which proposal seemed easier, and Yue wanted the sources to remain identifiable through that difference.

reservoir_ep04_015.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_015.text: The collective observer term allowed Yue to compare the offered public household schedules at the receiving table. Fu and Liu consented to that limited use after Qiu read its purpose aloud. Names of uninvolved neighbors stayed covered. Yue could see the exact work intervals beside the current turn numbers and ask both households about a possible exchange. The absence of the private factory stipend remained part of her actual term; the broader public comparison was the opportunity she had chosen in its place.

reservoir_ep04_016.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_016.text: Fu pointed to the three neighbor-assisted mornings and crossed them out as a future expectation. Liu marked the two market turns his household would offer for exchange, then asked Yue to copy only those dates into the proposal. She did. Their present consent supported this comparison, not every later public discussion of family care. Qiu retained the offered originals and accepted the limited comparative copy at the table. The plan could now be tested against actual overlapping hours rather than polished general claims about cooperation.

reservoir_ep04_017.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_017.text: The conditional factory term permitted Yue's numbered component extract and its specific receiving comparison, not the public observer's household record set. Qiu honored that narrower scope. Fu and Liu could still offer an ordinary public summary for their present proposal, which they did, while the detailed sheets stayed with the appointed receiver. Yue's useful question concerned the buffer's inspected cover and receiving method. She could compare the permitted component facts without quietly importing a private factory design into the household discussion.

reservoir_ep04_018.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_018.text: Jing inspected the ordinary cover arrangement under the basin's current order. Yue showed only the numbered fact she was allowed to offer, with its custodian's source label. The full reference sheet stayed outside the room. The cover's ordinary fit could be checked independently here; a familiar component did not need its old factory's authority to control a household turn. Qiu recorded which comparison Yue had actually seen. The schedule's detailed acceptance belonged to the household receiver, who would report its limited conclusion in the common meeting.

reservoir_ep04_019.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_019.text: Yue's winter-city departure supplied no transferred observer place or factory component mandate. Qiu therefore began with the ordinary public proposal and the basin's current consent process. Fu and Liu offered the hours relevant to their own possible exchange, without opening their full private sheets. Yue could help draw those offered intervals and ask what each meant. The grain appointment had made her copying work familiar, but the households still chose the scope. The independent route remained slower and free of a borrowed institutional endorsement.

reservoir_ep04_020.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_020.text: Qiu asked the appointed household receiver to compare the covered details and return a limited acceptance question. Yue waited while that actual work occurred. She could not certify the receiver's private comparison from the bench, and she did not need to. When Fu corrected an hour on the public drawing, Yue changed her own page visibly. Its modest scope was enough to prepare a useful proposal. A declined former post had closed shortcuts, rather than closing every possibility of ordinary collaboration with people willing to offer it.

reservoir_ep04_021.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_021.text: The earlier public conversation now needed its own source label. Yue's selected travel route determined whether she had heard Liu's offered account at the basin's first window or requested its written summary after the cart arrived. Qiu kept that distinction beside the current meeting's new observations. Today both households could speak for themselves. Their present consent did not retroactively make an absent traveler a witness. Yue set the older source apart from the current drawing before explaining the question that still depended on it.

reservoir_ep04_022.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_022.text: After waiting with the cart, Yue had missed Liu's first public conversation. She identified the offered written summary as her source for that interval and asked its appointed receiver to verify the one disputed hour. The receiver could do so during the next accepted desk period, while Liu answered the present question in person. Yue's first comparison therefore took longer. She had kept her equipment available through the journey and lost a direct conversation; neither fact needed to be erased to make her current help valuable.

reservoir_ep04_023.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_023.text: Liu noticed that Yue had not claimed to remember a discussion she had missed. He offered his current account more readily after that plain statement, then asked Tian whether the old date correction could be attached to it. Tian supplied its accepted public source. Qiu recorded the new consent and the remaining verification time. Her patient questions had made room for another honest conversation, though the missed morning and its witnesses remained beyond her reach. The water proposal could proceed after the real receiver supplied the limited check.

reservoir_ep04_024.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_024.text: Having taken the light-load foot connection, Yue identified the public conversation she had actually heard from Liu. She recalled asking whether the oven interval began before or after the first weighed delivery. Liu confirmed his offered answer and corrected the copied public summary, which had compressed the distinction. Her direct question saved the receiver a separate verification interval today. It did not make her private household witness. She had gained this conversation while losing the earlier equipment demonstration, and both consequences remained in the travel record.

reservoir_ep04_025.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_025.text: Liu recognized the visitor who had asked that useful small question at the first window. He offered her a piece of still-warm crust during the break and asked whether she would carry the corrected public wording back to Tian. She accepted the wording and shared the crust with Fu. Qiu recorded the present correction without treating familiarity as proof that every claim was true. The earlier walking decision now changed the meeting's actual sequence and a relationship at its table, while the household's covered pages remained with their proper receiver.

reservoir_ep04_026.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_026.text: On Day One Thousand Forty-one, Yue completed her fifth accepted grain day. Zhou had given her a narrow copying task so Tian could attend the household receiver under his actual traded interval. The current stock remained unchanged by the meeting's arguments. At lunch Tian returned with a flour mark on his cheek and a triumphant note: Liu's corrected oven hour had been accepted. Yue pointed to the mark. He tried to wipe it away with the wrong sleeve, making it larger, and she laughed before she could explain why.

reservoir_ep04_027.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_027.text: The day's three copper brought Yue's actual grain wages to fifteen. Zhou signed the accepted hours and asked whether the upcoming comparison would require any change to her next working day. It did not yet. Yue would keep the forty-sixth-day appointment unless the receiver authorized a specific substitution. Tian said he could help without another exchange because the next public interval fell after his shift. He sounded proud of having checked first. Zhou gave him the folded public copy and trusted him to deliver the version with the correct heading.

reservoir_ep04_028.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_028.text: Fu came to the meal house that evening carrying a little package for her brother. It held the ordinary replacement tie he had paid for after breaking her boots' old one. He had chosen a stronger material and sewn the ends himself. She rolled her eyes at his enormous knot, then admitted it would probably last longer. Yue remembered the wet boots by the lower-house door. A small obligation from the first conversation had actually been completed. They could laugh about its awkward appearance without treating the repayment as unnecessary because affection existed between them.

reservoir_ep04_029.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_029.text: Fu had been tempted to offer the neighbor another favor in exchange for water fetching. The neighbor had declined because her care appointment was genuinely full, not because the offered favor was too small. Fu heard the refusal and stopped bargaining. She told Yue the harder part was having to rethink a plan whose friendliness had made it feel dependable. An accepted temporary kindness could be precious and still end. Yue thought about her mother's actual care contacts and wanted the same freedom preserved for every person helping at home.

reservoir_ep04_030.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_030.text: Liu arrived with an ordinary bread board and demanded that everyone stop discussing his oven hours while the loaf was still warm. He cut uneven pieces for the table. Tian took the smallest, then was ordered to take a larger one because he had apparently become too serious about accounting for supper. The joke landed safely because the loaf was Liu's freely offered food, outside every contested fund. Yue ate with both hands around the crust. For a while the basin's people were simply hungry companions delighted by something good.

reservoir_ep04_031.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_031.text: On Day One Thousand Forty-two, Qiu walked the two proposed turn stations with their current keepers. Yue stayed within the visitor clearance and copied the offered ordinary observations. The exchange would move the same quantities between two times, while the buffer would hold Fu's accepted draw for later collection. Both plans needed a sound carrying route. The short step below the west wall had slickened after night frost. Qiu closed that approach temporarily and showed the longer accepted path. Whatever the household decided, speed would not make the closed step available.

reservoir_ep04_032.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_032.text: Fu measured the longer path's actual minutes with her own ordinary watch. Liu timed his bread preparation against the earlier turn he might receive. They corrected their proposals from those real intervals. The match still worked for the specific market mornings under discussion, but it was less convenient than their first table drawing had implied. Yue added the longer path to the common public sketch. A plan could survive new evidence by changing, rather than requiring every awkward fact to be dismissed as an exception to a beautiful first answer.

reservoir_ep04_033.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_033.text: Jing inspected the two offered covered jars and the carrying tray under the buffer proposal's actual ordinary purpose. Each jar held a checked ten litres at its marked usable line. Together they could hold Fu's existing twenty-litre allocation, with handling loss recorded rather than replenished invisibly. The covers fit, and the tray's sound handholds suited the accepted level route. Yue noticed how much of the proposal's safety came from plain objects and an actual worker's task. Her cultivation would supply none of the held water or the tray's carrying capacity.

reservoir_ep04_034.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_034.text: The qualified handling worker agreed to two four-hour intervals inside one ordinary day equivalent if the buffer proposal was ratified. The dates would match the two actual delivery collisions. Qiu recorded the worker's consent and the three-copper wage. The plan would not quietly require somebody else to fetch water for the family between those dates. Fu would collect the held allocation at the stated receiver, with a review before any further duty. Liu said this made the cost larger on paper than he expected. The worker said it made the cost visible.

reservoir_ep04_035.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_035.text: The turn exchange required no new paid handling interval, but it did require two households to accept a changed responsibility at their own doors. Liu's partner had agreed to the earlier collection after checking her work and sleep. Fu's brother had agreed to the later collection on the specified mornings. Neither household promised the arrangement forever. Qiu would register only the two trial turns and their review. Yue saw that the cheaper proposal had its own cost in altered routines, even though the water fund would preserve six actual copper.

reservoir_ep04_036.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_036.text: A third household worried that any exchange would invite everyone to move a turn each week. Qiu showed the bounded rule: named counterparts, unchanged quantities, current source checks and an accepted review. A later request would need its own comparison. The worried representative asked to inspect the published trial note before deciding whether to object. She read it slowly and accepted this limited case. Her question had improved the note. Yue liked the room more when concern could become a concrete correction rather than a person everyone had to defeat.

reservoir_ep04_037.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_037.text: The buffer had a different objection. A member thought six copper should instead remain for the next ordinary intake repair. Fu said she understood the competing use and wanted the household collision answered before another lost weighing shift. The receiver put both costs in the decision record. Nobody claimed the buffer was free because it used existing water, and nobody claimed the cheaper exchange could be accepted on Fu's behalf. The fund's members ratified either bounded allocation if its corresponding household proposal was completed and chosen for the actual trial.

reservoir_ep04_038.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_038.text: Liu asked Yue which proposal looked kinder. She said the word depended on whose actual inconvenience they meant. The exchange moved routines in two consenting households and preserved money. The buffer spent the remaining fund and kept the roster, while giving a worker a defined paid task and Fu a later receiving place. Liu took this seriously, then said the bread had been easier to divide. Fu answered that he had still made Tian take the biggest piece. The room laughed, and the decision remained difficult rather than becoming solemn beyond all proportion.

reservoir_ep04_039.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_039.text: On Day One Thousand Forty-three, the household receiver confirmed that either prepared plan could proceed under its stated standing consent. Yue had agreed to help carry one actual comparison through the trial and record what she herself observed. She could not perform both inside the accepted interval. Fu and Liu would keep their own responsibilities, and Qiu would ratify the selected bounded plan after checking its source. The winter-city record scope remained intact. Yue studied the two schedules, knowing that whichever she accepted would leave another useful, still unfinished task for somebody else to carry.

reservoir_calendar_choice.speaker: narrator
reservoir_calendar_choice.text: Helping the turn exchange would preserve the six copper and change the household roster on two market mornings. Yue's work would follow the actual collections and record any lost sleep or missed work the new hours revealed. Helping the buffer would commit six to its qualified handling, inspected jars and tray, while leaving the current roster unchanged. Yue would observe the two held allocations and their later receipt. Each choice came with a different unfinished risk. She chose which agreed proposal she would help make concrete, knowing that a pleasant conversation had not removed the cost.

choices.text: Help the consenting turn exchange; change two household mornings and preserve the six-copper fund.
Help the funded buffer; retain the roster and spend six on qualified handling and inspected storage.

reservoir_calendar_swap.speaker: narrator
reservoir_calendar_swap.text: Yue chose to help the bounded turn exchange. Qiu registered the two actual trial mornings after both households confirmed their standing consent. The twenty-litre allocations stayed unchanged, and the six copper remained in the water-assistance fund. Yue's accepted contribution concerned the ordinary timing observations and their public record. Fu tied the exchanged-turn note beside her brother's corrected work sheet. Liu took his household's counterpart home to the person who would actually wake for the earlier draw, rather than treating his own agreement as everybody's answer.

reservoir_ep04_042.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_042.text: On Day One Thousand Forty-four, Liu's partner reached the accepted station before the oven work began. The keeper checked the current source and filled the household's ordinary covered containers under the existing handling rule. Yue observed from the sound public place and recorded the actual receiving time. The earlier draw fit the bread schedule. Liu met his partner at the road junction with an empty carrying frame, and together they took the load by the accepted long path. Their cooperation had a real shape in the cold morning.

reservoir_ep04_043.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_043.text: Fu's brother arrived for the later exchanged turn after his accepted weighing interval. He brought the household's own checked containers and carried no grain load at the same time. The water reached the family without asking the neighbor to abandon her care appointment. Fu smiled so broadly that Tian teased her about having discovered a new realm called Being Home Before Dark. She flicked a flour crumb at his sleeve. Yue kept the joke out of the receiving record and remembered it afterward anyway.

reservoir_ep04_044.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_044.text: The first comparison showed no lost paid shift in either household. Liu's partner had, however, woken earlier than before, and the evening child-care interruption had shortened her actual sleep. She told Qiu at the agreed check instead of pretending the exchange had cost nothing. Qiu recorded the limit and asked whether she still accepted the second specified turn. She did, provided the household shared the ordinary evening task that night. Liu agreed to take that actual task, and the public water roster acquired no authority over their private family arrangement.

reservoir_calendar_buffer.speaker: narrator
reservoir_calendar_buffer.text: Yue chose to help the funded buffer trial. The members ratified six actual copper: three for one qualified handling equivalent, two for the inspected covered jars and one for the ordinary tray. Qiu issued the accepted work order and kept the original roster unchanged. The jars and tray belonged to the cooperative, not to Yue or Fu. The worker would fill Fu's existing allocation at its original turn and hand over the measured usable remainder later. A review would precede any further paid handling.

reservoir_ep04_046.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_046.text: On Day One Thousand Forty-four, the qualified worker filled the two checked ten-litre jars from Fu's ordinary twenty-litre allocation. He closed the accepted covers and took the sound longer path to the receiving shelf. Yue observed under the actual task clearance, keeping away from the load. A measured quarter-litre was lost in the accepted transfer, leaving nineteen and three quarters for later receipt. The worker wrote it down before the number could be mistaken for twenty. Neither an attractive plan nor a paid task made actual handling loss disappear.

reservoir_ep04_047.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_047.text: Fu collected after her weighing shift and checked the later receiving mark. The held water meant no neighbor had to leave a care appointment and no family worker lost a paid interval. To complete the household's planned kettle use, she drew a quarter-litre from her own already checked two-litre covered reserve. That left one and three quarters there. Yue wrote the actual household cost with Fu's permission. The buffer had solved a calendar collision by spending public handling money and a small measured part of a family's private stored margin.

reservoir_ep04_048.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_048.text: The worker compared the transfer method after the first accepted interval. Jing inspected the covers again under the existing order and found no leak; the loss had occurred at a hurried pour. She approved a slower ordinary receiving step within the tray's current clearance. No additional qi entered the water and no new jar purchase was charged. Fu wanted the second trial because the later collection had let her eat with her brother. She accepted the measured loss as a current cost, while asking that it be reduced rather than admired as an unavoidable sacrifice.

reservoir_ep04_049.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_049.text: On Day One Thousand Forty-six, between the two household trial mornings, Yue completed her sixth accepted grain day. Zhou paid its three copper after the numbered pages were checked, bringing her actual grain wages to eighteen. Tian had repaired the basket's crooked rim again and called it his most dependable colleague. Yue said it had tried to leave its post once. He replied that everyone deserved a journey, provided they returned with a receiving mark. They laughed while stacking the finished public copies.

reservoir_ep04_050.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_050.text: Fu came to collect a grain statement during the midday break. She described the first actual water trial in its own terms and asked Yue to attend the second comparison on the forty-eighth morning. Yue's next grain work remained on the fiftieth, so the agreed observation would fit her existing calendar. Fu also asked whether her brother's enormous new boot knot could be copied into Tian's growing basket story. Tian refused because a good basket should not be burdened with someone else's bad tailoring.

reservoir_ep04_051.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_051.text: Qiu checked the current source and path before the second specified trial. The first receiving record identified the selected exchange or buffer, its actual costs and the permissions still in force. The second comparison would follow that same bounded plan, unless a present unsafe condition required an ordinary stop. Yue prepared only its accepted observation sheet. A missing retained decision page would require the household receiver's source rather than a flattering guess. The next morning could show whether the arrangement survived another real work day.

reservoir_ep04_052.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_052.text: On Day One Thousand Forty-eight, the second exchanged morning proceeded under the checked current path and source. Liu had completed the offered evening task, and his partner reported a less interrupted night. Fu's brother collected after weighing again. Yue recorded the real times and asked both households whether any new work loss had been concealed by someone helping free of charge. They identified none in these two trials. The statement covered the inspected dates. A future delivery change would still require another actual comparison.

reservoir_ep04_053.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_053.text: At the public review, the households accepted a short extension only through the next stated market interval, with its own check before continuation. Their present result did not become a permanent assignment. The water-assistance fund still held six unspent copper, which could not be called a savings wage or spent on a new maintenance task without ratification. Qiu retained the selected roster counterpart. Fu thanked the neighbor for the earlier three temporary fetches and said the new arrangement would not depend on her continuing them.

reservoir_ep04_054.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_054.text: Yue saw Liu at the evening bakery closing. He was sweeping ordinary crumbs with a broom worn almost to its binding. He said the exchanged morning had let him keep the loaf warmer, and the evening task had made him less clever about offering other people's time. Yue asked whether he would write that second part in the public review. He laughed and said he preferred the accurate sleep account. She agreed. Their private conversation could hold an awkward lesson without turning it into somebody else's compulsory public confession.

reservoir_ep04_055.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_055.text: Fu's selected trial account named a changed roster, unchanged quantities, actual collections and the six-copper remainder. It also retained the altered sleep cost and the households' bounded response. Yue had helped a real arrangement whose advantages depended on consent and ordinary shared work. She had not purchased new equipment or used qi to erase the conflict. When she returned the public sketch, Fu kept her household original beside the paid grain sheet. The two papers now described a workable pair of mornings rather than the same old collision.

reservoir_ep04_056.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_056.text: On Day One Thousand Forty-eight, the second buffered allocation again began at twenty litres under the unchanged turn. The slower transfer lost one eighth of a litre, leaving nineteen and seven eighths for Fu's later receipt. She used the matching eighth from her household reserve, which now held one and five eighths. The worker completed the second four-hour interval and received the agreed three copper for one full equivalent. Yue checked the two actual receiving marks. A successful improvement had reduced a cost, not magically replenished the part already lost.

reservoir_ep04_057.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_057.text: At the public review, Fu wanted the later receiving arrangement continued through another collision. Qiu showed that the six-copper allocation was fully spent and the handling appointment complete. The inspected jars and tray remained available property, but a worker's future hours still needed a real new fund and consent. The members would decide that question at the next meeting. Fu accepted a dated gap rather than claiming that buying the objects had bought permanent labor. Her household retained the present unchanged roster until another arrangement was actually ratified.

reservoir_ep04_058.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_058.text: Liu brought bread to the review because he had heard the worker's second transfer had improved. He asked whether the jars were now Yue's instruments. Fu answered that they were ordinary cooperative containers, which had not acquired a cultivator owner by being useful in her presence. Tian laughed, then asked if he could carry the empty tray back by its accepted route. The custodian accepted that small returned-property task within his present paid interval. They all watched him walk extremely slowly, determined not to give another basket a story.

reservoir_ep04_059.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_059.text: Fu's selected account named the unchanged roster, spent six-copper fund, actual held receipts and the private reserve reduced from two litres to one and five eighths. It also retained the two improved handling results and the unfunded continuation question. Yue had helped an arrangement with real later access and a real cost. She returned every cooperative object to its appointed custodian. Fu kept the receiving copy beside the grain sheet, where two successful evenings could remain visible without being mistaken for an endless supply of somebody else's work.

reservoir_ep04_060.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_060.text: After the second trial, Qiu assembled the selected plan's actual record at the public table. The households' responses, real quantities and remaining work questions stayed attached. She did not merge the two possible mechanisms into one convenient success. Fu read the part that concerned her household, then corrected a copied character in her brother's name. Tian made the change visibly. Yue watched how much easier the correction had become after the room stopped needing every person to sound perfectly certain.

reservoir_ep04_061.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_061.text: On Day One Thousand Fifty, Yue finished her seventh accepted grain day and received three more copper, bringing completed wages to twenty-one. The month's ordinary stock comparison remained separate from the water-assistance fund. Zhou kept the grain house's actual source figures and returned the permitted household-copy counterpart to its appointed receiver. Yue's next four scheduled grain days lay in the following period. The term had space for them and for rest; no accepted hour had secretly been moved into a cultivation lesson.

reservoir_ep04_062.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_062.text: That afternoon, Fu and Liu argued cheerfully over whose bread-and-water joke should appear in Tian's private letter. Tian said neither had signed a performance contract and he intended to describe the basket instead. Fu threw another flour crumb, this time missing his sleeve entirely. Yue laughed with them, then grew quiet when she saw a private envelope waiting in her own receiving slot. The ordinary care question she had sent home now had an actual answer, and she wanted to read it away from the public table.

reservoir_ep04_063.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_063.text: Liu stopped her at the stair to ask whether she would stay for the next household review. Yue said she would compare the date with the work she had accepted. He nodded, then admitted he had wanted an easy promise because her presence had made the argument feel less lonely. She was glad he said it plainly. They could value a conversation without turning the person who helped once into permanent evidence that the institution cared.

reservoir_ep04_064.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_064.text: She took the letter to her paid room and opened it without asking Qiu to interpret it first. Her mother wanted to know when a visit might fit both their lives. She also had a sharp opinion about the tea at the last ordinary appointment. The account contained limits that had not vanished and decisions her mother was still making herself. Yue put the upcoming work dates beside the offered family days. The comparison would concern a real visit and missed opportunities, rather than a promise that enough cultivation could undo the old loss.

reservoir_ep04_065.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_065.text: In her room, Yue reread the family's offered days and pictured the doorway. She wanted to arrive with something better than another explanation of why work had kept her away. Yet a visit would require leaving some plateau opportunity unfinished and letting its receiver decide what could proceed without her. The wish became more serious when she stopped imagining that a higher stage would make every calendar fit. She kept the letter open beside tomorrow's page.

reservoir_ep04_066.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep04_066.text: Before the house's quiet hour, Yue returned Fu's offered private calendar page to its owner. The public receiving record retained only the scope each household had permitted. Her selected contribution was complete for this trial, with its real outcome ready for the next review. Tomorrow she would begin the family comparison while keeping the next accepted grain shift. At the doorway, Tian raised his repaired basket in a mock farewell. Yue answered with her empty ordinary cup, then went upstairs to write honestly about when she could come home.
